samples.summary: `mergeInlineStyle` copies and deletes arbitrary keys from an unvalidated style patch (no allow-list of InlineStyle keys)
samples.evidence: `mergeInlineStyle` does `{ ...base, ...patch }` and then `delete merged[key]` for every `Object.keys(patch)` entry, with no allow-list against the known `InlineStyle` keys (types.ts:146-186). Patches reaching `applyInlineStyle` are not always author-typed literals: the format painter and paste/import paths copy a style object lifted out of existing document content (which can come from a remote Yorkie peer, a pasted HTML/clipboard payload, or a DOCX import), so unexpected keys — including `__proto__`/`constructor` from a JSON-derived object — are carried into the stored run verbatim. I traced the actual pollution chain and it does NOT complete on this line: object spread uses CreateDataProperty and `delete` uses own-property semantics, so neither mutates `Object.prototype`; the one [[Set]]-based merge in the package (`Object.assign(style, TAG_STYLE_MAP[tag])`, packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:260,364) takes its source from an internal constant map and its tag key cannot be `__proto__` because the HTML parser rejects tag names starting with `_`. So this is unvalidated pass-through / hardening only, not a demonstrated exploit — an explicit `key in DEFAULT_INLINE_STYLE`-style allow-list (or `Object.hasOwn` guard) would close it permanently against a future [[Set]]-based consumer of the merged style.
